## Pass 1

Plate I (langdon1923_0042.jpg) read at II 47 and Plate II (langdon1923_0043.jpg) read line by line for III 1–38 at 2–6×; Langdon pp. 11–13 (langdon1923_0016–0018.jpg), transliteration, translation and footnotes, checked. Edits made by script (scratchpad rev1.py, rev1b.py), JSON loaded and dumped, no cuneiform retyped. gloss.json not touched.

### Changes

- III 4 (III 4–6) · n · major · "the -n- of ba-an- probably points to the place entered" misnames the element: -n- is the personal-class ('he') marker and cannot stand for the sea, a thing (that would be -b-) · sentence replaced: -n- is the personal-class element, cannot refer to the sea; its function in this intransitive verb of motion is unclear.
- III 17 (III 17–20) · i, l, n, morph gloss of lil₂-la₂ · major · "whose father was a lillu" is the modern rendering, not rebuilt from Langdon's reading (conventions: Langdon's reading is the base, the modern understanding goes in the note); l "a-lillu" likewise · i now "whose father was a fool (?)", l "a-fool(?)" (as kish-i II 14 'a poor man (?)'); note says the English gives Langdon's sense marked (?), keeps the lil₂ 'wind, phantom' alternative; the morph gloss no longer opens with 'lillu'.
- III 4 (III 4–6) · l, i · minor · e₃ rendered "went-out" / "came out to the mountains", where kish-i (Etana, II 16) renders the same verb UD.DU 'went up' and Langdon has 'went up unto the mountains'; "came" also adds a direction toward the speaker that ba- does not give · l "went-up", i "went into the sea and went up to the mountains".
- about · minor · same phrase "came out to the mountains" · now "went up to the mountains".
- about · minor · "The dynasty's total is one year less than the reigns as read, because one figure is itself partly restored" asserts a cause the copy cannot show · now: one year less; the only partly restored figure is the first king's; the notes report the difference rather than correct it.
- III 35 (III 35–36) · n · minor · "the difference lies in Meskiaggasher's 325" stated as fact · reworded: the only partly restored figure is the 325, a 324 would give 2,310, but the copy cannot show which; and that Langdon's own figures give 2,311 against his "This addition is correct". Arithmetic verified: 325 + 420 + 1,200 + 100 + 126 + 30 + 15 + 9 + 8 + 36 + 6 + 36 = 2,311; total as written 3 geš'u + 8 geš + 3 u = 1,800 + 480 + 30 = 2,310.
- III 7 (III 7–11) · morph gloss (-ga of the second unug{ki}-ga, III 8) · minor · labelled "genitive -a(k) 'of'" while the note says the force of this -ga (Uruk is the thing built) is unclear · gloss now: -a written -ga after the g of unug; here genitive or locative, force unclear (see the note).

Langdon's translations quoted ('At Eanna', 'was high priest', 'penetrated', 'the deified Lugalbanda', 'a fisherman', 'who built Erech') verified.
- House formulas: II 47 + III 1 give "In Eanna, Meskiaggasher … became king; he reigned 325 years"; later kings "X reigned N years"; "Twelve kings reigned 2,310 years"; "Uruk was smitten with weapons; its kingship was carried to Ur." Consistent with kish-i, as are the III 35 and III 37 notes (copied from kish-i's corrected wording), lemma strings (-šú, ba-gín, ni-ag, ib-ag, mu-bi, nam-lugal, -bi, -am₃, {d}, {ĝeš}, tukul, sig₃, ba-an-, lu₂, dumu, -ke₄) and the numeral encoding.
- Grammar labels checked against the forms: -ka (gen. -k + loc. -a), -am₃ copula, -ke₄ (gen. + erg.), -ga/-ma/-ba (gen. -a(k) after the stem consonant), mu-n-…-a (mu- + 'he' + nominalizer), -ni 'his', -še₃ terminative, -ba-ke₄, ib-ag (non-personal -b-, plural English by sense) — right.

### Sign findings (signs-cuneiform.json not edited)

- III 24 Utul: the UL key (glyph 𒌌, Unicode CUNEIFORM SIGN U GUD) is the best existing fit and is kept. The copy draws one sign, a corner wedge joined to a longer boxed sign, which matches U+GUD better than U followed by anything else; Unicode has no U TUL or UTUL character, and there is no TUL key. Needed only as a value: the UL entry's values list only "ul" — add "utul — Langdon 1923 (u + tûl) in Utul-kalam-ma (Weld-Blundell Prism III 24)" with signs.py when convenient. (This is a glossary value, not a missing sign.)
- Same kind of value gap, no new sign needed: TU (values tu, ṭu₂) is used here as ku₄ (Langdon tur); HAR as ḫur. Unicode has a separate CUNEIFORM SIGN KU4 (𒆭), not a key; the copy's sign in III 5 is hatched, so the plate cannot decide between it and TU, and TU = ku₄ is kept.

### Findings considered and refused

- Rename the morph lemma "{d}gibil-ga-mes" to "gibil-ga-mes" (its `g` excludes the determinative glyph, and Lugalbanda and Dumuzi have lemmas without {d}) · refused for now: gloss.json already keys the entry as "{d}gibil-ga-mes", which this pass may not edit; renaming here would break the build. Made and reverted in this pass. Pass 2 or the owner can rename it in both files together.
- gloss.json "lil₂-la₂" opens with "lillu —" · not mine to edit; pass 2 should bring it into line with the III 17 change (Langdon's 'a fool', marked uncertain).
- III 29 "dara₃(?)" in `reading`/`tr` while kish-i ships uncertain signs without (?) (II 32 U₃) · refused: the published Hammurabi parts ship "(?)" readings ("{lu₂}GA(?)", "[…]-tu(?)"), and the shape on the copy (corner wedge at left, hatched middle) does not confirm DARA₃, so the mark is honest.
- III 14 "ḪA.GUNU" in `reading` (the dot can suggest two signs) · refused: one glyph carries the whole name; no house notation for a gunû sign exists; the note and morph gloss say it is one sign.
- III 1 i "was lord and became king" gives two parallel copulas different English · refused: "became king" is the house formula for lugal-am₃; en is a title, and Langdon's 'high priest' is in the note.
- III 7 i "the one who built Uruk" vs kish-i II 35 "the man who" · refused: kish-i itself uses "the one who" for Etana (II 16); both stand.
- III 4 ab-ba with no written case ending rendered "into" · refused: the l marks it "(into)" and the note says the locative may be hidden in the -a.
- III 31 de₃ shown unbracketed although the sign is partly hatched · refused: Langdon prints de unbracketed and the note gives the doubt.
- III 3 2 u read where a third corner wedge may start the hatching · refused: only two are drawn whole; Langdon reads 2[5]; the note says the tens are at the edge of the break.

## Pass 2

Every gloss.json entry checked against units.json (notes and morph glosses), packet.md and Langdon pp. 11–13; units.json re-read in full. Edits by script (scratchpad rev2.py), JSON loaded and dumped; gloss.json key order kept.

### Changes — gloss.json

- __broaden__ ba-an- · major · the broadening said that with ba-an-ku₄ "the -n- may point to the place entered", the grammar rejected in pass 1 (the -n- marks a person, and the sea is a thing) · new text kept after the published entry and " · ": in intransitive verbs of motion (ba-an-ku₄ 'entered') the -n- has no clear 'he' to mark; its function there is uncertain.
- {d}gibil-ga-mes → gibil-ga-mes · key · minor · the lemma carried the {d}, though its `g` leaves out the determinative glyph, and Lugalbanda and Dumuzi (lugal-banda₃, dumu-zi), like the pilot's dumu-zi-sib, keep {d} as their own morph · key renamed together with units.json and new-lemmas.json; text now "written GIŠ.BIL, GA and MES (Langdon meš) after the divine determinative".
- lil₂-la₂ · gloss · minor · opened with "lillu —", out of line with III 17 now that it reads "a fool (?)" · now Langdon 'a fool' (lil-lá; 'the fool, imbecile, cripple', Akkadian lillu), KID + LAL, lil₂ also 'wind, phantom', so the sense is uncertain.
- ur-{d}nun-gal · gloss · minor · "another copy writes Ur-ᵈNun-lugal" gave as preserved what Langdon (fn. 4) prints as [Ur-ᵈNun-]lugal · now "another copy has [Ur-ᵈNun-]lugal (partly restored by Langdon)".
- -ka · gloss · style · tied to one form ("as in e₂-an-na-ka 'in the House of Heaven'") · example dropped, general sense kept.
- ab-ba · gloss · style · tied to one line ("Langdon takes the sea to be the Persian Gulf", his fn. 10 on III 5) · dropped; the III 4 note keeps it.

### Changes — units.json

- III 17 (III 17) and III 21 (III 22) · morph lemma {d}gibil-ga-mes · minor · (the same rename) · lemma now gibil-ga-mes; '{d}' stays its own morph (g [0]), as in lugal-banda₃ and dumu-zi; morph gloss reworded the same way.
- III 4 (III 6) · morph gloss of e₃ in ba-e₃ · style · gave Langdon's form as ĕ, but in this line he prints ba-ed · now "Langdon ed here, ĕ elsewhere".

### Checked and kept

- Coverage: every morph lemma in units.json is either in a published king-list glossary (king-list-antediluvian.json, king-list-kish-i.json) or in gloss.json; gloss.json has no orphan keys; new-lemmas.json equals the gloss.json keys; the broadening begins with the published ba-an- entry whole + " · ".
- Entries confirmed against the text and Langdon: mes-ki-aĝ₂-ga-še-ir (em = AĜ₂; fn. 9 Mes-ki-in-ga-še-ir), utu (ᵈBabbar, 'Shamash'), en, ku₄ (TU, Langdon tur 'penetrated'), ḫur-saĝ (diamond ḪUR on the copy), en-me-kar (fn. 11), unug, -ga (general), du₃ (KAK, dū), lugal-banda₃ (DA a complement), dumu-zi (fn. 1 Ab-ú), šu-ḪA.GUNU, uru, -ni, ḫa-a (bûr = A), kul-aba₄, -ba-ke₄ (gen. + erg., grammar right), utul-kalam-ma (U+GUD), la-ba-še-ir, en-nun-dara₃-an-na, […]-ḫe₂-de₃, me-lam-an-na, lugal-ki-aĝ₂, 12, urim₂. No invented modern forms; the modern readings named (ku₄, aĝ₂, Kuara, šu-ku₆) are flagged as such or as uncertain, as the notes do.
- units.json, read again in full: the grammar labels, l ↔ i, house formulas and the kish-i lemmas and numeral encoding are consistent after pass 1; no further findings.

### Findings considered and refused

- e₃ broadening (removed by the coordinator) · agreed: the published kish-i glossary already carries 'to go out, go up (also written UD.DU; Langdon ĕ)'.
- Names carrying a reign or a father in the gloss (en-me-kar 'son of Meskiaggasher', ur-{d}nun-gal 'son of Gilgamesh', utul-kalam-ma 'son of Urnungal') · refused: identifying a royal name by its lineage is general to the name, not to one line, and kish-i's name entries do the same; no reign figures are given.
- mes-ki-aĝ₂-ga-še-ir and en-me-kar giving Nippur spellings · refused: they are variants of the name, as in kish-i's ar-pi-u₂-um.
- "12": "twelve" brief · refused: it matches the format of kish-i's numeral entries.
